_why: Every failure of a section bound is SILENT. A truncated section is still a plausible string, and a positive assertion that happens to land before the cut still passes — which is exactly how a fence-blind bound hid 24,270 characters of `## Phase 5 (Implementation) sub-steps` from three live pins without a single test going red. So the mutants here do not break behaviour a normal assertion would notice; each one shortens or lengthens the extract, and only a test that reaches for text on the far side of the boundary can tell.

mutations.name: fence-tracking-removed
mutations._mechanism: Remove the authoritative scanner fence-state transition so a fenced column-zero heading ends the section. At GREEN anchor this in scripts/h_mad_doc_block_exec.py, not the removed local toggle.

mutations.name: section-no-longer-owns-its-subsections
mutations._mechanism: Remove the authoritative bounder level comparison so a section stops at a deeper subsection. At GREEN anchor this in scripts/h_mad_doc_block_exec.py, not the removed local regex.

mutations.name: offset-anchored-bound-runs-to-end-of-file
mutations._mechanism: `section_from` returns the rest of the document. Nothing fails and every positive assertion still passes — it is a byte window with no ceiling, which is strictly worse than the fixed window it replaced, because the pin now measures the whole file and can never distinguish 'documented here' from 'documented anywhere'.

mutations.name: missing-heading-returns-empty-instead-of-failing
mutations._mechanism: A renamed or deleted heading yields '' and every `in` assertion over it becomes False — which reads as a doc regression rather than a broken pin — while every `not in` assertion becomes VACUOUSLY TRUE. The loud assert is what keeps a missing section from being reported as a passing guard.

mutations.name: docsections-delegation-reverted
mutations._mechanism: Load the same callee under a private module name, breaking only the shared-import connection; only the wire pin should fail.

import re


def _fence_aware_end(text: str, start: int, level: int) -> int:
    off = start
    in_fence = False
    for line in text[start:].splitlines(keepends=True):
        stripped = line.lstrip()
        if stripped.startswith("```"):
            in_fence = not in_fence
        elif not in_fence and re.match(rf"^#{{1,{level}}} ", line):
            return off
        off += len(line)
    return len(text)


def _find_heading(text: str, heading: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    match = re.search(rf"(?m)^(?P<marks>#+) {re.escape(heading)}\s*$", text)
    return (match.end(), len(match.group("marks"))) if match else None


def titled_section(text: str, heading: str) -> str:
    """The named section's body, bounded by the next same-or-higher heading.

    `heading` is the text after the `#`s. The section OWNS its subsections: a
    bound that stopped at any heading would cut a `##` section short at its first
    `###` and every assertion about the later part would fail for the wrong
    reason.
    """
    found = _find_heading(text, heading)
    assert found, f"missing section {heading!r}"
    start, level = found
    return text[start:_fence_aware_end(text, start, level)]


def section_from(text: str, offset: int, level: int = 2) -> str:
    """From an arbitrary offset to the next heading at `level` or higher.

    For a pin anchored on a symbol rather than a heading — the case a byte window
    is usually reached for, because the anchor is mid-section and there is no
    title to name.
    """
    return text[offset:_fence_aware_end(text, offset, level)]
